turns.speaker: Andrew
turns.text: Perfect. So hello everyone. My name is Andrew Hoagland and I’m the cofounder and CEO of Vetd. Now the B2B market has never been more complex. There are now over 35,000 SAAS products in the market alone. And it’s an $83 billion industry. The vendors and the sales teams purposely don’t give out the pricing information. They gate it because they want to draw you into their sales process, get you on one or more calls and control the sales process from start to finish. Now I know this problem intimately because I helped create it. My background is B2B sales kind of the bad guy of the story.

turns.speaker: Andrew
turns.text: So we’ve had a lot of overwhelming demand recently. We’ve got a really big backlog of buyers trying to get on our platform. And we’re looking to raise $2 million to scale and meet those demands. And I look forward to questions

turns.speaker: Michael
turns.text: can you give us a real example of what you’re doing?

turns.speaker: Andrew
turns.text: Sure. So one of our users recently needed to buy a new retail operations system. they're like, all right, we need it to inventory management, we're on Shopify, we have multiple warehouses, we need to be able to do order fulfilment and returns. So what we say is, great. We already have this database of all these vendors. They have all the top vendors curated for them without having to do anything. They get it down to their final maybe one or two options, usually one. And then they say, great, now I'm ready to spend time with this vendor

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: Can't you, is it... Can you just be like, hey. It's like going to the used car lot and you be like, you know what, I have this amount of money, you're going to give me a car. Like, I refuse to talk to anybody. And like I've done this. And I hate the talking to people aspect of all this.

turns.speaker: Andrew
turns.text: You're an ideal user.

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: Yeah. Thanks. But can't you like, can't you just skip it?

turns.speaker: Andrew
turns.text: I wish the answer to that question was yes. And if it was yes, I wouldn't be standing here

turns.speaker: Michael
turns.text: And how are you paid?

turns.speaker: Andrew
turns.text: So we actually only monetize the vendor side Vendors pay a subscription to us, they're on our platform and as many deals as we could possibly drive them, they have a set...

turns.speaker: Michael
turns.text: But if they don't pay you, they don't get on your platform and you don't recommend them.

turns.speaker: Andrew
turns.text: That's not true. We want to make sure the buyers always win. So the most important thing is the buyers have access to the platform and the best options

turns.speaker: Michael
turns.text: So how much do I pay to come on to your platform?

turns.speaker: Andrew
turns.text: As a buyer? Nothing.

turns.speaker: Michael
turns.text: No, no. As a seller, as a vendor.

turns.speaker: Andrew
turns.text: So our subscription model will be anywhere from 12 to 25,000 annually. just based on size of the company right. We have to remain this impartial third party, so by having a very transparent vendor pricing system, we don't have to worry about anyone thinking, oh, are the big vendors paying you more? This is exactly how much they're paying us. This is why they're paying us. And it's all transparent and visible.

turns.speaker: Phil
turns.text: But they do have to worry about vendors paying versus those that don't pay.

turns.speaker: Andrew
turns.text: Right. But the beauty...

turns.speaker: Phil
turns.text: There's still that distinction.

turns.speaker: Andrew
turns.text: Totally. Totally. But the beauty of this system is now that we have the numbers and the leverage, this is one of the reasons this had never been solved before, is you never really had the leverage. If we came out and we're like, we have five buyers, no one is going to change their process. We now have at least 900 ready to go and that number is growing rapidly.

turns.speaker: Michael
turns.text: Right.

turns.speaker: Andrew
turns.text: And now the part I'm really excited to get about is what we're calling kind of the community aspect, which is why we have this big backlog.

turns.speaker: Phil
turns.text: Yeah Why is there a backlog? Why can’t you get them on your platform right away?

turns.speaker: Andrew
turns.text: So when we started we would go one to one. We’d get a buyer, We’ve learned how to get buyers in large groups, as opposed to one off. they would come on to our platform, we’d onboard them. So over the last three weeks, we started to reach out to some VCs both in and out of our network and say hey, we want to come to you and bring you a community version of Vetd, it'll be free for you, it'll be free for all of your buyers. And the response from VCs has been incredible. Over the last three weeks, we have eight VCs on board, representing over 900 portfolio companies.

turns.speaker: Phil
turns.text: When you bring in a community, are you offering them discounts as well?

turns.speaker: Andrew
turns.text: That is one of the value props to the communities. We're saying, hey, most VCs or communities - it doesn't have to be a VC - do not have a dedicated resource to thinking about this. They maybe have an Excel sheet We are saying, we'll have an entire sales arm whose sole focus is on making we have vetted vendors with aggressive discounts for your community. And the bigger we grow that sales team, the higher that number becomes. In the end it's the entire market.

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: How many of those portfolio companies, like have they actually rolled it out to those companies?

turns.speaker: Andrew
turns.text: Well, so that's why I'm standing here. We can't keep up with the demand that we've now created. But with $2 million we can. Cos we'll have a self-serve product. It will be that we can onboard them as soon as they login.

turns.speaker: Michael
turns.text: How long will that take to build?

turns.speaker: Andrew
turns.text: I do not like to give out estimates, but we are planning...

turns.speaker: Michael
turns.text: You're very much a sales guy, but like a little less sales guy. Like start giving us the facts.

turns.speaker: Andrew
turns.text: We think if we get the money in the near future, two to three months after the money is in the bank we'll be able to roll out consistently and onboard in large batches.

turns.speaker: Michael
turns.text: This reminds me of Commerce One way back in the days, like in the 90s. You might remember these. Where you would actually launch these bidding platforms and it would actually bid down vendors and stuff. Eventually a lot of us vendors and stuff in the software world said, we're not even going to participate in this. We're not going to be in this bidding process. There was a kind of a revolt How do you get around that?

turns.speaker: Andrew
turns.text: So we don't do it that way. We don't try to create bidding wars, per se. We try to say, all right, put forth your pricing model, put forth your transparency. The vendors gonna then engage in a conversation with you. And then it's just like...

turns.speaker: Michael
turns.text: And you guys step to the side then?

turns.speaker: Andrew
turns.text: Yes.

turns.speaker: Michael
turns.text: Okay. Oh yeah, that sounds a little better.

turns.speaker: Andrew
turns.text: So then we step out of the way

turns.speaker: Phil
turns.text: So now in a sense you're going to the vendors and also saying, hey, in addition to a subscription fee I need a discount from you?

turns.speaker: Andrew
turns.text: Exactly.

turns.speaker: Phil
turns.text: But to Michael's point, doesn't that create that kind of competition among vendors for who's going to provide the biggest discount...

turns.speaker: Andrew
turns.text: Sure.

turns.speaker: Charles
turns.text: That already exists. We have 150 companies in our portfolio and every time Amazon changes the AWS discount, we go to Google and Google changes the AWS discount. They want the business.

turns.speaker: Phil
turns.text: Yeah. No. I was just thinking about whether the vendors want, will want to participate in this marketplace if it's a competitive, a race to the bottom in terms of pricing.

turns.speaker: Charles
turns.text: No. But they have to. Like, I mean, I guess it's sort of like nobody ever wants to offer discounts unless they have to. But in most of these categories, the customer has, I mean, we all invest in SAAS companies. Name a SAAS category that has one vendor. There isn't one, right? So in all these categories there are many, many, many vendors. Some of whose products are awfully similar.

turns.text: Sounds like you should hire Charles.

turns.text: Look I'll be honest. I should probably just be honest. We're talking, we've been talking to them about using Vetd for our platform because I'd say a third of our Slack channel messages are - we're looking at Lever or Greenhouse. What should we use? What did you pay? How did you get a discount? We're looking at Mailchimp versus XYZ thing. What are the pros and cons? And so for us... We have another company in our portfolio, Stackshare, that focuses on the sort of tech...

turns.speaker: Michael
turns.text: You started to use them? Vetd.

turns.speaker: Charles
turns.text: We haven't rolled it out yet. We are part of that 900 backlog. And it's just because...

turns.speaker: Jillian
turns.text: Are you funding them too?

turns.speaker: Charles
turns.text: We have not made an investment decision. We have a company in our portfolio, Stackshare, that does the tech stack piece. I haven't sorted out in my mind whether we can have two of them in the same portfolio.

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: We actually have one that's... So it's called Venture App and it started off trying to do this but more on the services side. So legal, accountants, etc So I'm sitting here having the same...

turns.speaker: Phil
turns.text: Yeah. I am too. We're investors in IT Central Station.

turns.speaker: Charles
turns.text: I'm basically interested in taking down G2 Crowd. So I don't know whether I can do that with one bullet or two bullets. I just - and no offence to the G2 Crowd people - I just think… I don't think that's the way we should buy software today.

turns.speaker: Michael
turns.text: How is that? What do they do?

turns.speaker: Charles
turns.text: It's like a... Think about it like Yelp for software except the nature and how some of those reviews are generated is um...

turns.speaker: Jillian
turns.text: So unethical

turns.text: every week I get an email from G2 Crowd paying me to write reviews. I haven't.

turns.text: Really?

turns.text: Every single week.

turns.speaker: Jillian
turns.text: See. Unethical.

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: That is crazy.

turns.speaker: Andrew

turns.speaker: Charles
